diagram_math_checks.objects: Paths w_{2r}(t)=0 and w_{2r+1}(t)=sin(pi t)e in C([0,1];H), with ||e||_H=1.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The Statement fixes these exact paths and unit-vector hypothesis. The plot shows their real coefficients a_n(t), not a scalar coordinate on all of H.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The horizontal variable runs from t=0 to t=1 and the coefficient heights are 0 and sin(pi t).
diagram_math_checks.justification: TikZ positions are (5t,2 sin(180t)); its trigonometric argument is in degrees, yielding exactly the coefficient sin(pi t). The vertical tick at geometric height 2 is labeled coefficient 1.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Both endpoints are zero; the odd-path maximum is 1 at t=1/2.
diagram_math_checks.justification: sin(0)=sin(pi)=0 and sin(pi/2)=1. The two black endpoint markers lie at (0,0),(5,0); the peak marker lies at (2.5,2), with t=1/2 and coefficient=1 ticks, matching Statement and proof 1.1.

The Facts define the supremum metric. Since ||e||_H=1, the difference norm is |sin(pi t)|, at most 1 and equal to 1 at t=1/2. The vertical measurement arrow and top guide encode this supremum height, agreeing with proof 1.2.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Terminal evaluation ev_1:C([0,1];H)->H sends each displayed path to 0.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Every continuous H-valued path has a value at 1 in H; the two endpoint computations in proof 1.1 give precisely zero. No injectivity or converse convergence claim is drawn.
